objective: Re-review the repair commit on release/0.3.0/refactor/host-neutral-cli against the earlier code and security findings, so the PR can close.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-cli; repair diff (generated bundle excluded): /home/user/holyagent-notes/pr2-repair.diff; the repair commit is HEAD on top of ee51233.

Earlier findings to check closed: help failing on an invalid HOLYAGENT_HOST; PI_SESSION_LINK (and the claude.ai link pattern) swallowing a closing parenthesis; PI_GENERATED_FOOTER quadratic backtracking on 'generated with pi(' plus many ')'; PI_NAME stripping any 'Co-authored-by: Pi' regardless of address; hard-coded 'workflow:'/'pi-workflow:' prefixes duplicated in host.ts; assignment record loading the whole config so a bad HOLYAGENT_REUSE_TTL_MINUTES breaks recording; reconcile reading the host itself (resolved by a stated choice); pi record and reports help still describing Claude hooks and journals.
constraints: Judge the repair diff against those findings and any new issue it introduces. Read-only. Findings blocking or non-blocking with file:line and a reproduction or trace. Report in under 300 words.

result:
result: All earlier findings are closed. The repair adds no blocker; 6 optional notes below.

changed: none (read-only)

checks:
- `bun test` in packages/runtime -> exit 0, 928 pass, 0 fail.
- Ad hoc timing of `cleanMessage` with 20k, 40k and 80k character inputs ("pi(" plus many `)` or `(`, many spaces) -> at most 2 ms each and growing linearly, so no backtracking blowup.
- The generated bundle contains the new symbols (`rg -c` finds 7 matches). I did not rebuild it or run `mise run verify`.

blockers: none

notes (all optional):
1. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/message.ts:33` (`SESSION_LINK`, `PI_SESSION_LINK`): a Markdown session link `[text](url)` now leaves `[text]()`, and the new test asserts that residue. The old `\S*` pattern also left residue (`[text](`), so this is not a regression. Matching the whole `[text](url)` would clean it fully.
2. `packages/runtime/src/cli/assignment.ts:315`: `assignment record --failed` still fails under an invalid `HOLYAGENT_HOST`. It failed that way before the repair too, because the old code loaded the whole config. The host lookup could move into the `--agent` branch.
3. `packages/runtime/src/cli/program.ts:92`: help under an invalid `HOLYAGENT_HOST` falls back to Claude's wording, exits 0 and gives no warning. The repair states this choice and tests it, and it matches how `failed()` already behaved.
4. `packages/runtime/src/domain/host.ts:1`: it imports two constants from `directive.ts` at runtime. There is no cycle: `directive.ts` imports `host.ts` as a type only, and `errors.ts`, `assignment.ts`, `specialists.ts` and `route.ts` do not import `host.ts`. The coupling is cosmetic.
5. `packages/runtime/src/domain/host.ts:79`: the pi `reportsNote` says reports reads "Claude workflow journals only for now", but `journalResults` in `cli/report.ts` makes no host check. It is guidance rather than enforcement, and that is acceptable as a stated choice.
6. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/message.ts` (`PI_AGENT_NAME`): `Co-authored-by: Pi <x@example.com>` now stays in the message. This is a deliberate, tested narrowing, so I read it as a choice rather than a defect.
7. `packages/runtime/tests/vcs-message.test.ts:93`: the linear-time test uses a 1000 ms wall-clock bound. The repair measures about 2 ms at 80k characters, so it is unlikely to flake.

evidence:
- Findings closed: help under a bad host now uses `hostForText` (program.ts:92-139, tested in host.test.ts); the link patterns stop at `)` (message.ts:33-34); the footer regex is linear (timing run above); `PI_AGENT_NAME` requires "Pi Coding Agent" or a pi.dev address (message.ts:35-41); the prefixes are now the `directive.ts` constants (host.ts:56,75); `record` reads only the host through `agentHostOf` (assignment.ts:314, test passes with a bad TTL); `reconcile` keeps its host-only read with a comment (overview.ts:178); pi help now has `recordNote` and `reportsNote` (tested).
- No new issue: the full runtime test run passes (928 pass, 0 fail, exit 0). I found no regression or vulnerability, only optional notes 1-7.
- findings: none blocking; optional notes 1-7 above.
